subject.title: [Bug]: Secret provider crash-loop exhausts 1Password service account rate limits

question: What startup failure policy should OpenClaw own when active exec-backed SecretRefs fail under a supervised gateway service?
rationale: Automation should not choose between fail-fast security, degraded/unready availability, retry timing, circuit breaking, provider-specific rate-limit detection, or new config surface without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Bounded generic startup guard
options.body: Add a provider-agnostic startup guard that retries transient SecretRef failures with bounded backoff and then stops repeated external provider calls while surfacing a clear local recovery path.

options.title: Document supervisor limits only
options.body: Keep runtime fail-fast semantics unchanged and document launchd/systemd restart-throttling plus external caching resolver guidance for quota-sensitive secret providers.

options.title: Provider/plugin-owned caching first
options.body: Route 1Password batching/caching to ClawHub or external resolver plugins and only add core APIs if those implementations expose a missing OpenClaw seam.

recommendation.title: Bounded generic startup guard
recommendation.body: Add a provider-agnostic startup guard that retries transient SecretRef failures with bounded backoff and then stops repeated external provider calls while surfacing a clear local recovery path.

likelyOwner.reason: The provider-based external secrets and runtime SecretRef activation history most directly maps to the policy decision.
